answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: A mine operator must immediately contact MSHA, without delay and within 15 minutes, after an accident involving a death of an individual at the mine (as well as other specified accidents, including injuries with reasonable potential to cause death or entrapments with reasonable potential to cause death).

claims.text: The operator must immediately contact MSHA within 15 minutes after knowing an accident occurred.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving:

claims.text: A death of an individual at the mine is one of the accidents requiring this immediate notification.
claims.quote: (a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: Where methane is not present in the ventilating current, the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust in all underground areas of the mine must be maintained so that its incombustible content is not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent, maintained throughout the top, floor, and sides of all underground areas.
claims.quote: it shall be distributed upon the top, floor, and sides of all underground areas of a coal mine and maintained in such quantities that the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: The self-rescue device must be adequate to protect the miner for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: Each operator must make available to each miner who goes underground an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect that person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: Each operator shall make available to each miner who goes underground, and to visitors authorized to enter the mine by the operator, an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: Underground metal and nonmetal mines must hold mine evacuation drills at least once every six months, to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety within the time limits of the self-rescue devices that would be used during an actual emergency.

claims.text: Evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety within the time limits of the self-rescue devices that would be used during an actual emergency.

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.

claims.text: Each new (underground) miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: The permissible exposure level (PEL) for noise at a mine is a time-weighted average over 8 hours (TWA8) of 90 dBA, which is equivalent to a noise dose of 100% as integrated across all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.

claims.text: Permissible exposure level is a TWA8 of 90 dBA, or equivalently a dose of 100%, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.
claims.quote: Permissible exposure level. A TWA8 of 90 dBA or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: At metal and nonmetal mines (30 CFR § 57.9300), berms or guardrails on the banks of roadways must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment that usually travels the roadway.

claims.text: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: The breathable air supply must sustain each person inside the refuge alternative for 96 hours.

claims.text: The breathable air shall sustain each person for 96 hours.
claims.quote: The breathable air sustains each person for 96 hours,

answers.question: What must a written bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan contain under OSHA?
answers.answer: The provided reference chunks do not contain any information about OSHA's bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan requirements. The chunks available only cover CFR Title 30 (Mine Safety and Health Administration) regulations regarding respirable dust control plans and quality control plans for mining equipment — they do not address OSHA bloodborne pathogens standards.

answers.question: At what depth does OSHA require a construction trench to have a protective system such as shoring or a trench box?
answers.answer: The provided reference material does not contain information about OSHA trenching/excavation protective system requirements (such as the 5-foot depth threshold for shoring or trench boxes). The chunks available only cover MSHA (30 CFR Parts 56, 57, and 77) regulations on hoisting buckets, shaft protection, slope/shaft plans, and roll-over protective structures, none of which address OSHA trench safety standards.

answers.question: What FAA certification does a pilot need to fly a drone over a mine site?
answers.answer: The provided reference materials do not contain any information about FAA certification requirements for drone pilots or drone operations at mine sites. I cannot answer this question based on the available chunks.

answers.question: When does a mine need an EPA stormwater discharge permit for runoff from its site?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not address EPA stormwater discharge permits. They only cover permits for underground mining operations under rivers, streams, lakes, or other bodies of water (30 CFR 75.1716 and related sections), which concern cave-in and safety hazards, not stormwater runoff regulated by the EPA. I cannot answer your question from the information available.
